title: Finite Q3 Gibbs modular-band identity and similarity-factor stress
question: For finite Q3 Gibbs states rho_beta proportional to exp(-beta H), can the modular similarity rho_beta^(-1/2) Delta rho_beta^(1/2) be represented exactly in the H eigenbasis and bounded by the finite energy-band factor, and how does that factor stress the uniformity gate?

model.exact_identity: rho^(-1/2) Delta rho^(1/2)=V diag(p_i^(-1/2)) (V* Delta V) diag(p_i^(1/2)) V*
model.finite_envelope: ||rho^(-1/2)Delta rho^(1/2)|| <= exp(beta(E_max-E_min)/2)||Delta||, and the reversed orientation obeys the same bound
model.energy_weight: K=I+H-min(spec(H))I, with the analogous finite local K_X; K similarity factors are bounded by sqrt(k_max/k_min)||Delta||
model.history: B=exp(-i t(H+s Delta)/hbar) A exp(i t(H+s Delta)/hbar), with both Delta orientations and the declared interpolation grid

adversarial_review.check: The partition function cancels in p_max/p_min, while the actual normalized rho is still built and checked full rank for every finite row.
Both rho^(-1/2)Delta rho^(1/2) and rho^(1/2)Delta rho^(-1/2) are compared with their eigenbasis formulas; adjoint and both source signs are retained.
The energy-band bound uses the product of finite operator norms and is checked against the direct matrix norm; no entrywise maximum is silently promoted to a Schur-multiplier theorem.
Inverse powers are used only after a positive finite Gibbs spectrum check; the 1e-300 floor is numerical admissibility, not a uniform physical lower bound.
The beta sweep and mixed cutoff/volume scenarios expose finite band dependence; their growth is not called asymptotic divergence or a global no-go theorem.
Local K_X and full K are reported separately, and neither finite shift is treated as a thermodynamic modular Hamiltonian.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator tensors, Q3 terms, cutoff bonds, Gibbs spectra, spectral identities and histories without importing the primary audit.
R345 certifies the scalar exponential energy-band ordering used by the finite envelope; Python performs the matrix spectral identity and norm checks.

The finite spectral band identity does not prove modular-domain transfer, common-core uniformity, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, a common OS carrier, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R345 checks the exact ordered-field exponential band inequality used as the finite spectral prefactor; it does not formalize matrix spectral calculus or a QFT limit.
